VI): each drone carries a camera and onboard companion compute (Jetson Nano in AirSim bench / UP Core in Holybro PX4 prototype) running a lightweight DRL Neural Scheduler and optionally executing DroNet locally; a ground edge server hosts per-drone containerized DroNet instances managed by a centralized Resource Allocator and Container Controller (zero inter-UAV communication).
dnn_or_workload: Navigation DNN: DroNet augmented with a Spatial Pyramid (SP) pooling layer after residual block 4 to accept dynamic input resolutions {448x448, 336x336, 224x224, 112x112, 56x56} (Fig. 7 p. 5; scheduler uses {448x448, 224x224, 112x112}). Dataset: Mid-Air synthetic/low-altitude drone flight video dataset (80 min, ~420,000 frames, Sec. V-C p. 7) for DRL training; HSDPA mobile 3G wireless bandwidth traces (B1-B4, Secs. V-C & VIII-C); AirSim 'Coastline' 1200 m route (16 turns) and real 300 m university campus route.
partition_or_collaboration: NONE at DNN layer level (J=0): whole DroNet model runs either entirely onboard (o=0) or entirely inside a drone's edge server container (o=1); adaptation adjusts input resolution r and JPEG compression ratio j rather than splitting DNN layers.

Objective: maximize QoN Q = sum I(|theta_pre - theta_gt| <= eps) / tau (Eqs. 1-2 p. 4) on single drone and average QoN across n drones.

solution_method: Drone side: A2C (Stable-Baselines3 PyTorch, RMSProp lr=7e-4, gamma=0.99, 2-layer [128,128] Actor and [64,64] Critic, 6x10^5 offline lookup-table iterations) with EIE state encoder (Sec. architecture_and_uav_role: Three-tier multi-UAV-edge-cloud hierarchy (Ocularone VIP platform, Secs. 3.1-3.3, Figs. 3-4): Tier 1 consists of 2-4 'buddy' drones per VIP acting strictly as aerial camera sensors and PD flight-control actuators over WiFi (running zero onboard DNNs); Tier 2 is a VIP-carried GPU-accelerated edge base station (emulated Jetson Nano / field Jetson Orin Nano) hosting the Java scheduler and synchronous Python/PyTorch gRPC DNN service; Tier 3 is a shared AWS Lambda cloud FaaS deployment serving all drones of all VIPs.
dnn_or_workload: Six pre-loaded whole vision DNNs (Secs. 7 & 8.1 Table 1): HV (Hazard Vest detection, YOLOv8n), BP (Body Pose, ResNet-18 + SVM), DEV (Distance Estimation to VIP, YOLOv8n + linear regression), DEO (Distance Estimation to Objects, Monodepth2), CD (Crowd Density, YOLOv8m), and MD (Face-Mask Detection, SSD). Video workload: pre-recorded Tello drone campus video streams (emulation) and live 720p 30 FPS Tello feeds (field test); network variability uses real IISc->Mumbai WAN measurements plus NS-3 4G cellular traces of 7 SUMO-simulated drones (Fig. 2).
partition_or_collaboration: NONE at DNN layer level (J=0): whole pre-loaded DNN models execute atomically either on the base-station edge gRPC service or as AWS Lambda FaaS functions over 1 s (~38 kB) video segments (Sec. 3.3, Sec. 4).
decision_variables: Per-task placement & queue order: execute on edge (EDF priority t'_j + delta_i), migrate/offload to cloud FaaS (FIFO / trigger-time priority queue), steal back to edge on slack, or drop; GEMS greedily migrates pending edge tasks of lagging model mu_i to cloud when incremental completion rate alpha^x_i < alpha_i. Objectives (Sec. 4 Eqs. 1-2, p. 13-14): maximize total utility gamma = sum gamma^j_i + sum gamma_bar_i (combining QoS utility beta_i - t_i*kappa / -t_i*kappa and tumbling-window QoE utility beta_bar_i when >= alpha_i fraction finish within deadline delta_i in window omega_i) and maximize on-time task completions.
objective: See source-located decision/objective field; no pooled effect
solution_method: Deterministic online scheduling heuristics (Secs. 5-6, Alg. 1): DEMS (EDF edge queue + score-based edge-to-cloud migration S^j_i = gamma^E_i - gamma^C_i + cloud-to-edge work stealing ranked by (gamma^E_i - gamma^C_i)/t_i), DEMS-A (adds circular-buffer sliding window w=10, threshold eps=10 ms, cooling period t_cp=10 s for cloud latency adaptation), and GEMS (adds tumbling-window omega=20 s QoE monitoring and greedy rescheduling).
mobility_failure_or_recovery: Mobility: in field test (Sec. 8.8), 1 DJI Tello tracks a walking proxy VIP via PD controller (~2 ms command delay, 100 m LoS WiFi range); in Fig. 2c, 7 mobile nodes in SUMO+NS-3 generate cellular bandwidth traces; VIoLET emulation models WiFi links between drone containers and edge containers (no drone crash or mid-flight wireless disconnect modeled). Channel/variability: Linux tc trapezium latency (0-400 ms) and NS-3 4G bandwidth traces between edge and AWS cloud (Sec. 8.5). Failure handling: deadline misses incur negative utility (-K or -K_hat) or task dropping (0 utility); at 30 FPS EO in field test, HV task expiration causes Tello safety auto-landing (DNF, p. 36). Drone/edge battery energy is explicitly not modeled as an optimization constraint (Sec. 9 p. 38).
evaluation: Three evaluation modes: (1) Real-world AWS Lambda ap-south-1 FaaS (1-5 GB RAM) + VIoLET container emulation on Intel Xeon 6208U (30 vCPUs, 128 GB RAM, Ubuntu 18.04) mimicking Jetson Nano (4 vCPUs, 4 GB RAM per edge; 0.1 vCPU, 100 MB per drone; 7-28 drones/host, up to 84 drones/4 hosts, Secs. 8.1-8.6); (2) Sleep-emulated alternate edge/cloud latencies WL1 & WL2 for GEMS (Sec. 8.7 p. 32: 'replacing the DNN execution with just a sleep function'); (3) Real hardware field test with 1 DJI Tello (80 g, 720p@30 FPS) + 1 Jetson Orin Nano over 150 Mbps 802.11n WiFi + AWS Lambda (Sec. 8.8).
baselines: Emulation (Sec. 8.2): CLD (cloud-only), HPF (edge-only highest utility/time first), EDF (edge-only EDF), EDF (E+C), SJF (E+C), SOTA 1 (adapted Kalmia + D3), SOTA 2 (adapted Dedas), plus ablations E+C -> DEM -> DEMS -> DEMS-A -> GEMS. Field test (Sec. 8.8): EO (Edge-Only), E+C, DEMS.
reported_outcomes: QoS Utility gamma^j_i (dimensionless normalized benefit minus amortized edge/FaaS cost, Eq. 1); QoE Utility gamma_bar_i (Eq. 2); Task Completion Rate (% of tasks finishing within deadline delta_i); Edge Utilization (%); Drone Jerk J(t) = da/dt (m/s^3) and Yaw Error (pixels, Sec. 8.8).
